title: Sesterce to invest $10bn in 600MW AI data center campus in Jämsä, Finland
source_used: The Next Web (citing Sesterce and Yle)
key_facts: Sesterce plans to invest more than €10bn in an AI data center campus at the Kaipola site in Jämsä, central Finland, where UPM closed a paper mill in early 2021.
First phase 200 MW, building due to start this year; a second phase would raise capacity to 600 MW; Sesterce aims for over 1 GW in Finland over time.
About 2,000 jobs during construction and about 300 permanent jobs.
Sesterce aims to add 1 MW of new renewable energy for every MW the campus uses over ten years, and to set up a €10 million local fund.
Kaipola Green Port owns the site; its chair told Yle that negotiations to sell the whole site to Sesterce are well underway.
Local officials welcomed the plan but noted permits are still required.
Google said in September it would spend €13bn on AI infrastructure in Finland in 2027 and 2028; a Finnish regulator this week ordered Google to stop clearing forest at two planned sites.
quote_evidence: Building work on the first phase, with 200 megawatts (MW) of capacity, is due to start this year.
Local officials have welcomed the plan, but they noted that permits are still required.
Over the next ten years, it aims to add one megawatt of new renewable energy to the grid for every megawatt the campus uses.
why_it_matters_hint: Large new AI campus in Finland, still dependent on permits and a land sale.
notes: Announced by Sesterce; also carried by Yle, Le Monde, Helsinki Times. DCD headline says $10bn.
